value: Company stated AI-driven memory and storage growth was outpacing industry supply in Q3 FY2026, with robust DRAM and NAND demand and constrained supply contributing to higher pricing and improved profitability across the portfolio.
location: MD&A Industry Conditions / Memory and Storage Demand

value: Company stated customers are increasingly seeking committed long-term access to advanced memory technology and supply; strategic agreements provide supply assurance and pricing visibility to customers and greater visibility and stability to Micron.

CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said Micron is aligning its organization to meet customer needs in an AI-enabled future and expressed confidence in Manish Bhatia and Scott DeBoer to guide the company through the next phase of innovation and growth.

Manish Bhatia appointed President and Chief Operating Officer; expanded accountability includes global operations and business units and operating P&L spanning capital investment, manufacturing execution, customer demand, pricing and delivery.
Scott DeBoer appointed President and Chief Technology and Products Officer; responsibilities include technology and product roadmap, Micron Research Labs and customer technology requirements.
Sumit Sadana transitioned from Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer to Senior Advisor to the CEO.
FY2025 revenue $37.378B versus $25.111B FY2024; company reported +49%.
FY2025 operating income $9.770B and operating margin 26%, versus $1.304B and 5% FY2024.
Q3 FY2026 revenue $41.456B versus $23.860B Q2 FY2026; company reported +74% sequentially, driven by DRAM and NAND sales increases.
Q3 FY2026 consolidated gross margin 85% versus 74% Q2 FY2026; company attributed improvement primarily to DRAM/NAND ASP increases, with execution and favorable mix also contributing.
Debt carrying value $5.72B at 2026-05-28 after $9.38B of debt repayments during the first nine months of FY2026.

value: On 2025-10-06 YMTC filed multiple patent infringement complaints against Micron and subsidiaries in the Eastern District of Texas, the English High Court, the Unified Patent Court in Dusseldorf, and Munich Regional Court concerning certain 3D NAND, LPDRAM, NAND and DRAM products; complaints seek injunctions, attorneys' fees, damages and costs.

On 2026-03-06 Nextech Semiconductor filed a patent infringement complaint against Micron and MSP in the Western District of Texas alleging six U.S. patents are infringed by certain DRAM, NAND and SSD products and seeking an injunction, damages, attorneys' fees and costs.
On 2026-05-21 the appeals court affirmed the German Federal Patent Court invalidity ruling for one Netlist patent; the appeal concerning the second patent had not yet been decided.

Q3 filing states HBM demand may fluctuate; HBM requires more wafers and cleanroom space per bit than conventional DRAM, and a shift of capacity from HBM to conventional DRAM if HBM demand weakens could increase conventional DRAM supply and pressure pricing.
